q: In the training data, `plan` has Basic 1,802 rows, Plus 1,435 and Premium 763. Which index does `StringIndexer` give to Basic?
o: `0.0`, because it is the most frequent
`1.0`, because indices start at 1
`0.0`, because it comes first alphabetically
`2.0`, because it is the cheapest plan
e: The default `stringOrderType` is `frequencyDesc`: the most frequent category gets index 0. Alphabetical order only breaks ties, and meaning plays no role.

q: `region` has 4 categories in training. With `handleInvalid="keep"` and the default `dropLast=True`, what does an unseen value such as `Islands` become after `OneHotEncoder`?
o: An error at transform time
A vector of size 5 with a 1 in the last position
An all-zero vector of size 4
A null vector
e: The unseen value gets the extra index 4. The encoder knows 5 indices, drops the last one, and the last one is exactly that unknown bucket, so the vector has 4 zeros.

q: A column `size` has the values Small, Medium and Large, and the order matters. What is the right encoding?
o: `StringIndexer`, because it keeps the natural order
`OneHotEncoder` without `StringIndexer`
`TargetEncoder` with `targetType="continuous"`
An explicit mapping such as `F.when(c == "Small", 1).when(c == "Medium", 2)...`
e: `StringIndexer` orders by frequency, not by meaning. Only a mapping you write yourself guarantees Small < Medium < Large.

q: When is feeding `StringIndexer` indices directly (without one-hot) to a model reasonable?
o: For linear regression, because it is faster
For Spark ML tree models that read the category metadata, with `maxBins` at least the number of categories
Never, Spark ML models reject indices
Whenever the column has more than 100 categories
e: Spark ML trees use the nominal metadata that `StringIndexer` attaches and split on groups of categories. A linear model would read 0 < 1 < 2 as a real numeric order.

q: You fit `TargetEncoder` on the whole table before splitting, and validation AUC jumps. What happened?
o: Smoothing was too low
The test labels leaked into the encoded feature
`targetType` should have been `"continuous"`
Nothing: target encoding is expected to help this much
e: Target encoding computes the mean label per category. Fitted on all rows, the test rows' own labels are baked into their feature. Fit it on the training set only.
